subject: ela
cluster: Research to build and present knowledge
intro: Seventh graders gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard citation format. Paraphrasing means restating an idea in your own words.

items.prompt: What is the difference between QUOTING and PARAPHRASING?

steps: Quoting uses the source's exact words in quotation marks; paraphrasing restates the idea in your own words.
So quoting is word-for-word; paraphrasing is in your own words.
solution.answer: Quoting uses exact words; paraphrasing restates the idea in your own words.

items.prompt: Do you need to cite a source when you PARAPHRASE it?

steps: Paraphrasing still uses someone else's idea.
So yes, you must still cite it.
solution.answer: Yes, you must still cite it.

items.prompt: How can effective SEARCH TERMS improve research?

steps: Specific keywords find more relevant results.
So good search terms find relevant, accurate sources faster.
solution.answer: Specific keywords find more relevant, accurate sources.

items.prompt: Using exact words in quotation marks is ____.
Restating an idea in your own words is ____.
You must ____ a source even when paraphrasing.
